Scope decision recorded: migrate src/core/** (bands, pressure, rolling, trend, normalize, policy, maintenance, safe-point, presets, scheduler, config), src/providers/** (the telemetry provider contract and the node:os-backed collectors), src/audit/decision-log.ts and src/types/**; DROP src/dsh/** entirely because it is the Hns/DeepSeek plugin binding the mission exists to remove. The donor never executes a restart, which stays true here and is verified by test.

Host Mech claimed the MB-005 migration stage. Digital-City claim commit 89d506e7a791b9c90006d2a4f19dd4d73c4c897a pushed to City main with no write conflict. Selection was made against the latest City main: MB-001 migration is complete and unclaimed for verification (Mech is not its migration host), MB-003 is claimed by Alien and MB-004 depends on MB-003, so sequence order selects MB-005. Implementation branch mission/MB-005-host-health created from utopia main c7ef3cd1c6be0155332d03afc3607dfdbf49c205.

Parity oracle established. The donor is TypeScript with zero runtime dependencies; installing typescript 5.7.2 into the git-ignored donor checkout and running its own tsc produced lib/**/*.js (31 files) that executes on plain Node. That gives an executable golden reference: the ported Utopia module can be differential-tested against the donor implementation on identical synthetic inputs, which is far stronger parity evidence than ported test vectors alone. The donor's own tests also run against this build.

TEST_FAIL: three root capability tests hard-coded manifest positions. tests/capability-registry.test.mjs used m.districts[0] and m.districts[2] and asserted an absolute unbridged count of 1; tests/capability-adapters.test.mjs used manifest.districts[0] and asserted catalog.length===6 and 5 AVAILABLE. Declaring the new 02-engineering/03-host-health-station building changed the census, so all three failed. This is the same class of fragile fixture that MB-002 already had to repair, and it is a latent defect on main that every future Mission declaring a district or building would trip. Failure receipt: .runtime/evidence/mission-book/MB-005/run-1/tests/root-tests-before.txt

REPAIR_APPLIED: made the three fixtures census-relative instead of position-dependent. They now use m.districts.at(-1) for the district under test, count unbridged capabilities relative to a baseline taken before the fixture mutates the manifest, and assert added-parser entries by capabilityId suffix rather than by absolute catalog size. The properties under test are unchanged - qualified identity per district/building/module, pending state for an unbridged module, and that all five bridged adapters still execute - but they can no longer break merely because a later Mission declares another district or building. After the repair pnpm test is 58/58 and node city/test-all.mjs is 212/212.

TEST_PASS: host-health-station module suite 83/83 (82 unit/parity + the differential harness). The differential harness drives BOTH the ported module and the COMPILED donor (dsh-health-scheduler @ 985e2b7, built with its own tsc) through 110 seeded scenarios: 110 agreed, 0 disagreed, 916 ticks, 3433 per-metric entries, 89 decisions, 8 restart requests actually exercised, 41 decisions carrying a refusal reason, actions THROTTLE and PAUSE_NEW_WORK both exercised. The donor's own 155 tests also pass against that compiled build, so the oracle is known-good. Receipts: .runtime/evidence/mission-book/MB-005/run-1/tests/

OWNER_INTERVENTION: real donor bug found and deliberately NOT fixed. dsh-health-scheduler src/core/bands.ts bandKeyOf() never returns :warn for a lower-is-worse metric, because rampEndpoints returns best>worst for that polarity so the second test (value <= worst) is unreachable. Reproduced against the compiled donor: bandKeyOf('recovery_rate', 0.6, {warn:0.8,critical:0.3}) === 'recovery_rate:critical' when it should be ':warn'. higher-is-worse is unaffected. Effect: for those metrics the band clock starts at the warn endpoint, so crossing warn->critical already satisfies the sustain gate. CHOICE: port it exactly and pin it with a naming test, because MIGRATION_ONLY forbids changing donor semantics and a silent fix would break differential parity and change when a gate opens. RECOMMENDATION: the City owner needs a superseding decision before this is treated as intended; the fix is two lines but it is a behaviour change. Recorded in DONOR.json donorBugsFound.

Repair R1, evidence completion on the same branch and inside the mission boundary. The module test suite passes 83/83 with 0 skipped only when the donor build exists. As delivered, the differential harness skips, because it needs the compiled donor at .runtime/evidence/mission-book/MB-005/donor-health/lib/index.js, which was absent. The differential harness then ran for real: 110 scenarios compared, 110 agreed, 0 disagreed, across 916 ticks, 3433 per-metric entries, 89 decisions, 8 restart requests and 41 decisions carrying a refusal reason. No branch content changed.

Test evidence on the branch. Module suite: 83 tests, 83 pass, 0 fail, 0 skipped, including the differential parity harness at 110 of 110 scenarios. No test was skipped, deleted or relaxed. The whole city suite and the rest of the acceptance matrix are recorded in a later event.

Real telemetry run, phase A of scripts/mb005-health-pilot.mjs, on this host. The port sampled the machine through its own provider graph (defaultEnvironment, HardwareProvider, RuntimeProvider) and measured SEVEN real metrics: cpu_usage 0.19 percent, ram_total_bytes 34101420032, ram_available_bytes, ram_used_ratio, uptime_seconds 227248, process_rss_bytes and handle_count. Driving the scheduler with those real readings gave coverage 0.6 with the honest unknown dimensions runtime, worker and computer_use_ui - a real host does not supply every modelled dimension, and the port says so instead of inventing numbers.

Real unknown-missing, sustained-pressure and anti-flapping scenarios, phases B and C. With a registered provider that has measured nothing, coverage is 0, SIX dimensions are reported unknown, and the metrics map marks NOTHING as zero: missing telemetry stays unknown rather than becoming a fabricated 0. Holding ram_used_ratio above its critical band for longer than its own 120000 ms sustain window produced exactly ONE escalating decision, THROTTLE, a member of the closed ladder. Then oscillating the metric across the band for six crossings produced ZERO further escalating decisions: anti-flapping suppressed the repeat.

Bounded action request and the existing consumption surface, phases D and E. The decision ladder tops out at REQUEST_SYSTEM_REBOOT, a request; the shipped restart adapter refused both application and system restart with accepted false and state rejected, reason dsh-restart is not installed in this profile; and a scan of all 20 module sources found no restart or reboot execution primitive, with providers.mjs the ONLY file that can spawn a process at all (and only for its injected telemetry helper probe). For consumption: the same real telemetry was accepted by the EXISTING node channel, POST /api/v0/node/register returned 200, and GET /api/v0/nodes returned it unchanged - cpu 0.2 percent, memory total 34101420032 bytes, uptime 227248 seconds, online true. Those are exactly the fields the existing Web and Android device panels render. No dashboard was created.

Reconciliation with the Migration Report, read only after the findings above were written and recorded, per rule 9. AGREEMENTS, and they are strong: my independent run reproduced the reports differential line exactly, 110 scenarios compared, 110 agreed, 0 disagreed, 916 ticks, 3433 per-metric entries, 89 decisions, 8 restart requests, 41 decisions carrying a refusal reason; the whole-suite figure 212 of 212, pnpm test 58 of 58, rooms 67 of 67, promotion history 10 records and bilingual docs SYNCHRONIZED all reproduce; the no-restart-execution audit agrees; and my real-telemetry run independently produced the SAME coverage 0.6 and the SAME three unknown dimensions, runtime, worker and computer_use_ui, that the report records from its own live consumption driver.

Reconciliation differences. D1: the report section 9 lists the compiled donor oracle and a consumption driver under the git-ignored evidence area, but on the delivered branch that area was EMPTY - no donor-health build and no run-1 directory - so the differential harness, the reports strongest evidence, skipped by default. I rebuilt both (R1) and added a committed pilot (R2). D2: the reports real-telemetry evidence therefore was not reproducible from the branch; mine is. D3: the report section 6.4 records the same census-fragility repair I found on MB-002 and MB-004 - the identical fix now exists on a fourth branch, so merge must union rather than take either side wholesale. D4: the report section 8.4 explicitly hands the two-host clause to the Verification Host, which is the tension recorded separately.

The two-host clause, recorded as a mission-design tension rather than silently resolved. The gate reads: two hosts each run real telemetry through the normal, unknown-missing and sustained-pressure/anti-flap scenarios. Rule 5 permits exactly ONE verification host per mission and forbids a third; this session has one machine. Reading 1, per participating host role: the migration host has its own recorded runtime evidence on the branch (a RUNTIME_PASS event and the reports live consumption driver) and this host has the real run recorded above, so the clause is met across the two participating hosts. Reading 2, two physical machines: not satisfiable here. Both readings are recorded rather than one asserted, following the identical precedent Mech recorded for MB-006 section 5.2. No second machine was fabricated and none was claimed. Owner may rule.

Verification gate assessment. MET: bounded action requests only, proven by running and by source audit; the existing Web and Android telemetry surface reads real status and history with no new dashboard; real telemetry exercised across normal, unknown-missing, sustained-pressure and anti-flapping scenarios; donor parity by executing the compiled donor over 110 scenarios. TENSION RECORDED: the two-host clause, under both readings, with no fabrication. Repairs stayed inside the branch: a git-ignored donor build plus one committed pilot script, no production file changed. The one donor bug the report describes, bandKeyOf never returning warn for a lower-is-worse metric, is ported rather than fixed and is recommended for an Owner decision, which I confirm is the right call under MODE=MIGRATION_ONLY.
